prior_blocking_findings_recheck.evidence: New src/app/settings/__tests__/page.test.tsx covers all four required behaviors: (1) loading state shown before and during in-flight fetch, asserting fetch called with '/api/billing/subscription' and 'Loading your subscription' text present both before and after effect runs while the fetch promise is unresolved; (2) free-tier flow (isPremium:false) renders 'Upgrade to premium' button, absence of 'Manage subscription', clicking POSTs '/api/billing/checkout' and redirects window.location.href to the returned url; (3) premium-tier flow (isPremium:true) renders 'Plan status: active', formatted currentPeriodEnd date, 'Manage subscription' button, absence of 'Upgrade to premium', clicking POSTs '/api/billing/portal' and redirects to returned url; (4) error state for both a rejected fetch and a non-2xx response, asserting an element with role='alert', a generic actionable message ('We couldn't load your subscription details. Please refresh to try again.'), no crash (render does not throw), and explicit assertions that raw details ('low-level network failure', 'Request failed with status 500') are NOT present in rendered text — directly matching the contract's 'never exposes raw error details' invariant.

webhook.test.ts now asserts currentPeriodEnd: new Date('2026-09-27T12:00:00.000Z') inside the expect.objectContaining block for both the customer.subscription.updated test (past_due mapping) and the customer.subscription.deleted test (canceled mapping), matching the current_period_end: toUnixSeconds('2026-09-27T12:00:00.000Z') set on the Stripe event fixtures. This exercises the exact unix-seconds-to-Date conversion and pass-through the ticket's period-end access semantics depend on (resolved ambiguity #5). A dropped, zeroed, or mis-converted currentPeriodEnd would now fail these tests.

unchanged_findings_reference: All other findings (test_quality_notes, acceptance_criteria_coverage for the four unaffected criteria, and overall assessment of subscriptions.test.ts, subscription.test.ts, checkout.test.ts, portal.test.ts, entitlements.test.ts) are unchanged from round 2 and remain valid — see delta_of file for full detail; those files were not touched in this round.
test_quality_notes_delta: page.test.tsx uses a lightweight custom React-hook shim (manual useState/useEffect stand-ins) rather than @testing-library/react, but it faithfully drives the real component tree returned by SettingsPage() and correctly re-renders after state updates; the button-finding and text-collection helpers correctly traverse the JSX element tree including nested children. This is an unconventional but valid testing approach that exercises real component logic, not mocks of the component itself.

webhook.test.ts currentPeriodEnd assertions use exact Date equality (new Date(iso string)) inside expect.objectContaining, correctly isolating the currentPeriodEnd field without needing to restate the full upsert payload.
recommendation: Accept. Both round-2 blocking gaps are resolved by the delta: SettingsPage now has thorough behavioral coverage (loading, free/premium button gating and redirect wiring, dual error-path handling with no raw-error leakage), and webhook tests now assert currentPeriodEnd propagation for both subscription.updated and subscription.deleted events. No new gaps introduced by the delta. No further blocking issues identified.
